reach.rationale: The app builds exclusively on long-stable Nuxt/Vue APIs; it deliberately avoids the experimental surface Nuxt 4.6 shipped (Vapor, vite-server, usePreviewMode) despite being on the newest release.

app/app/composables/useApiBase.ts:1-9 — runtime-config access centralized in one composable
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain; the closest thing (direct h3 imports) is a two-line, copy-pasted pattern confined to the 404 paths of five page files.

app/package.json:6-10 — dependency set is just nuxt/vue/vue-router, nothing pre-release
justification.rationale: No experimental or recently-unstable APIs are used at all, so there is nothing unjustified; the conservative API surface is itself a defensible choice for code meant to be owned for years.

findings.issue: setResponseStatus imported directly from h3 (same import in pokemon/[name].vue:2, moves/[name].vue:2, abilities/[name].vue:2, types/[name].vue:2). Nuxt 4.6 introduced nuxt/server as the recommended portable import surface; direct h3 imports are exactly what will need edits at the Nuxt 5 (h3 v2 / Nitro v3) jump.
findings.suggestion: Migrate the five call sites to import server utilities from 'nuxt/server' (one file at a time, to avoid the mixed-import NUXT_E8012 error). Not urgent — h3 imports remain stable in 4.6.

findings.issue: vue and vue-router are pinned explicitly alongside nuxt; Nuxt manages these versions itself, and a hand-pinned vue-router can drift from the version Nuxt expects.
findings.suggestion: Drop vue/vue-router from dependencies and let nuxt resolve its own Vue versions.

summary: This app uses zero experimental, preview, RC, or canary APIs — it's built entirely on the long-stable Nuxt core (useAsyncData, useHead, useState, useRuntimeConfig, file-based routing, layouts) against the current stable Nuxt 4.6.x line, with no experimental config flags. The only forward-compat nit is importing setResponseStatus from h3 directly in five page files where Nuxt 4.6's new nuxt/server surface is the recommended path for surviving the Nuxt 5 upgrade. As a risk profile this is about as safe as a Nuxt app gets.
